items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Her name was Connie Wittingham. She was a little girl that used to carry me to school who I met a lot later, after I grew up.

ctx.x: St. Augustine’s – that’s about 15th and V [streets], or something like that?

Yeah, it’s right in there somewhere. I’m trying to think. Yeah, it’s right there. I used to walk – be able to walk to school from wherever we were living at the time. I remember that. The teachers – sisters always - I remember them being nice and kind to me, the Dominican sisters, I think they call it. That was it for me. I was right in the neighborhood. I could go to school there. I remember one little girl that lived in the neighborhood. My mother used to get her to take me – by the time I got to go to school –…

whole time. I never went to another school, like a middle school or any of that. I just went from kindergarten all the way out until I went to high school. I don’t know what I can think about in between that.
